LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD defines a standard source download from the project's GitHub release page: an AppImage file is fetched using a direct HTTPS link with a pinned version and a matching `sha256sums` entry. The source URL is constructed predictably from the declared `pkgver`, and no command substitution or dynamic code execution is involved in fetching it. There are no top-level commands, `pkgver()` function overrides, or variable assignments using command substitution that would execute arbitrary code during sourcing.

The only executable code at the global scope is static variable assignment. No `eval`, `curl | bash`, `wget`, or other dangerous constructs appear in the PKGBUILD. The `source` array uses a named assignment to download the AppImage directly, which will be extracted later during the build phase—but extraction is safely deferred until after this gate, and `--nobuild --noprepare` ensures it won't happen now. The `noextract` and `sha256sums` entries further confirm intent to handle the binary safely and reproducibly.

This file poses no risk during `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare`. Fetching the source and parsing the PKGBUILD involves only safe, static evaluations.
</details>
<summary>
Safe sourcing and verified source fetch
</summary>
</security_assessment>

The source is a single AppImage file, which is extracted in the package() function using the --appimage-extract flag. The extracted contents are then installed into the package directory under /opt/omikuji, and a wrapper script is created in /usr/bin to launch the application.

The build process includes a symlink to the host's KDEPlasmaPlatformTheme6.so for theme integration, which is a known workaround for AppImages lacking certain Qt/KDE integration plugins. While this introduces a dependency on the host system's Qt6 installation, it is not inherently malicious. The desktop file and icon are installed with standard permissions, and the Exec line is patched to use the wrapper script.

All operations are transparent, reproducible, and confined to the package's own files. The checksum is provided and matches the expected AppImage. There are no network calls at runtime, no obfuscated code, no unexpected file operations, and no evidence of data exfiltration or remote code execution. The package follows common AUR practices for AppImage-based packages.
</details>

<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD's global/top-level scope contains only standard variable assignments with no command substitutions, inline execution, or other code that would run during sourcing. There is no `pkgver()` function. The single `source` entry fetches an AppImage directly from the package's own declared upstream (`https://github.com/reakjra/omikuji`), which is entirely expected. A concrete `sha256sum` is provided (not SKIP), so the download will be verified. The `noextract` directive prevents automatic extraction of the AppImage. All potentially sensitive operations (AppImage extraction, file installation, symlink creation) are confined to `package()`, which `--nobuild` prevents from running. Nothing executes at source-fetch or parse time that raises concern.
</details>

There are no suspicious network calls, no obfuscated commands, no use of `eval`/`base64` in unexpected contexts, and no exfiltration of local data. All operations are scoped to `$srcdir` and `$pkgdir`.
